Introduction

Executive Summary

Al Fateh finished 12th of 18 on 37 points (9W-10D-15L). The underlying data tells a more hopeful story: a top-8 team by process that finished bottom-half by outcome. Four coachable failures explain 12th: wasteful finishing, a poor away record, conceding in two clear time windows, and dropping too many points to weaker teams.

The headline: We didn't finish 12th because of the giants - we finished 12th because we wasted our chances (-14.2 vs xG, the league's worst), collapsed away (12 pts on the road), conceded in waves at 15-30 & 75-90 min, and crucially dropped points to the teams below us (just 4 wins in 12 vs the bottom six). All four are coachable without major spending.

The real lesson: We took just 4 points from 8 games vs the Top 4 (expected - they were the class of the league) but only 17 points from 12 games vs the Bottom 6 - 4 wins, 5 draws, 3 losses. A top-half team must punish the weaker sides, and we didn't. Beating the bottom six more convincingly is the single biggest, most realistic points gain for next season.

Deep Dive

The Finishing Gap - Why 12th

Goals minus xG: -14.2, the league's worst. ~2.5 goals = 1 point, so recovering half is worth +5 to +8 points - the gap from 12th to 7th/8th.

xG created vs goals conceded - league map

My central pitch

The chances are already created. We need a clinical finisher and a finishing-focused training methodology. The points are on the training pitch.

Section 4

Playing Identity & Game Model

What we are

Aggressive, vertical, pressing - top-5 press, 3rd in counters, strong interceptions.

The refinement

Keep the press; add controlled build-up (fix worst pass accuracy) and concentration drills for the leak windows.

Match-up plan

Press & counter the top-4; dominate & be clinical vs the rest - especially away.

Identity in one line: "An organised front-foot pressing team that defends as a unit, attacks with width and crosses, manages games to the whistle, and finishes the chances we create."
Section 5

Recruitment Plan

Priority 1 - A clinical finisher

TargetClubGoalsxGG-xGConv%AgeValue €
Stand-out: Khalid Al Ghannam (Al Ettifaq, 25, ~€0.5m) - 13 goals from 6.1 xG. Saudi national, ideal age.

Priority 2 - Goalkeeper upgrade

Our keeper is -2.9 prevented goals. M. Rodak (+6.1) and Samuel Portugal (+6.2) lead the league.

Priority 3 - Retain & promote

Build around Bendebka, Vargas, Naif Masoud. Minutes & role clarity, not spending.

Conclusion

Summary & Recommendations

1
Fix the finishing. Half the -14 gap = ~+5-8 pts. Methodology + one clinical striker. HIGHEST IMPACT
2
Punish the weaker teams. Only 17 pts from 12 games vs the bottom 6 - the biggest realistic gain is winning these convincingly. BIGGEST GAIN
3
Win away. Just 12 away points. A road game-plan & mentality. QUICK GAIN
4
Close the leak windows. 40% of goals conceded in 15-30 & 75-90 min. Concentration + game management + fitness. DEFENCE
5
Keep the identity, add control. Retain press & counters; fix pass accuracy. Build around proven assets. GAME MODEL
Closing message: "This is not a 12th-place squad - it's a top-8 squad that left points on the pitch through finishing, away form, game management and failing to beat weaker teams. All are coachable."
